target: Het bed is zacht en comfortabel.
english: The bed is soft and comfortable.
tip: After a linking verb like is, the adjective stays uninflected, so it stays zacht, never zachte.

target: Het lichte huis heeft grote ramen.
english: The bright house has big windows.
tip: Before a plural noun the adjective always takes -e, so ramen gives grote ramen.

target: Eerst moeten we het formulier invullen.
english: First we must fill in the form.
tip: After a modal a separable verb stays whole at the end: moeten ... invullen = have to fill in.

target: Ik begrijp niet wat je bedoelt.
english: I do not understand what you mean.
tip: In a wat-clause the verb moves to the end, so it is wat je bedoelt, not wat bedoel je.

target: Ik ga een film kijken vanavond.
english: I am going to watch a movie tonight.
tip: Gaan plus an infinitive expresses a near-future plan, like going to: ga ... kijken is am going to watch.

target: Mijn tante bakt altijd de lekkerste taart.
english: My aunt always bakes the tastiest cake.
tip: The superlative adds -ste after de, so lekker becomes de lekkerste, meaning the tastiest.

target: De tuin heeft een vijver met vissen.
english: The garden has a pond with fish.
tip: A short vowel doubles the final consonant in the plural, so vis becomes vissen, not visen.

target: Het kantoor is op de vijfde verdieping.
english: The office is on the fifth floor.
tip: Most ordinals up to nineteen add -de, so vijf becomes vijfde for fifth.

target: Het cadeau is ingepakt met rood papier.
english: The present is wrapped in red paper.
tip: In a separable verb's participle the ge- slots between prefix and stem, so inpakken becomes ingepakt.

target: Het moment was kort maar heel bijzonder.
english: The moment was short but very special.
tip: Heel before an adjective means very: heel bijzonder is very special.

target: Het project kost naar schatting veertigduizend euro.
english: The project costs an estimated forty thousand euros.
tip: Currency and measure words stay singular after a number, so it is veertigduizend euro, never euros.

target: Hij volgt de bordjes naar het stadscentrum.
english: He follows the signs to the city center.
tip: Diminutives form their plural with -s, so bordje becomes bordjes, not bordjen.

target: Waarschijnlijk komt hij morgen niet naar kantoor.
english: He probably won't come to the office tomorrow.
tip: Dutch uses the plain present for the future when a time word is there, so komt with morgen means will come.

target: Kort daarna vertrok de trein richting Maastricht.
english: Shortly after that the train departed towards Maastricht.
tip: Vertrekken is a strong verb, so its past changes the vowel: vertrekken becomes vertrok, not vertrekte.

target: Midden in de nacht werd ik wakker.
english: In the middle of the night I woke up.
tip: Wakker worden uses worden, to become, for a change of state: werd ik wakker means I woke up.

target: Bij uitzondering mag je vandaag langer opblijven.
english: As an exception you may stay up longer today.
tip: Mogen means to be allowed to, so mag je marks permission, not ability the way kan je would.

target: De bomen verliezen hun bladeren in de herfst.
english: The trees lose their leaves in autumn.
tip: A doubled long vowel drops to single when the syllable opens in the plural, so boom becomes bomen.

target: Het gedicht is geschreven door een beroemde dichter.
english: The poem was written by a famous poet.
tip: In the passive, door marks who does the action, so geschreven door de dichter means written by the poet.

target: De kerk staat al eeuwen in het dorp.
english: The church has stood for centuries in the village.
tip: Dutch pairs the plain present with al for something ongoing, so staat al eeuwen means has stood for centuries.

target: Heeft u een vegetarisch gerecht op het menu?
english: Do you have a vegetarian dish on the menu?
tip: Yes/no questions start with the verb, so it is Heeft u ...?, with the subject after the verb.

target: Mag ik u iets vragen over de openingstijden?
english: May I ask you something about the opening hours?
tip: Mag ik ...? is the polite way to ask permission: Mag ik u iets vragen.

target: Kun je me even helpen met deze doos?
english: Can you help me with this box for a moment?
tip: Even softens a request into just a moment or real quick, so helpen with even sounds lighter than a bare helpen.

target: Met de trein reis je snel door het land.
english: By train you travel quickly through the country.
tip: By a vehicle is met de plus the vehicle, so met de trein means by train, not per or op.

target: Ruim op tijd kwamen wij aan op de luchthaven.
english: We arrived at the airport well ahead of time.
tip: Aankomen is separable; in a main clause the aan drops to the end: kwamen wij aan, we arrived.

target: De kat zit op het dak van het huis.
english: The cat sits on the roof of the house.
tip: For an animal in a spot Dutch prefers zitten, so the kat zit op het dak where English says sits or is.

target: De haven van Rotterdam is de grootste van Europa.
english: The port of Rotterdam is the largest in Europe.
tip: With a superlative, van means in, so de grootste van Europa means the largest in Europe.

target: De salade bestaat uit sla, tomaat, komkommer en ei.
english: The salad consists of lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and egg.
tip: To consist of is bestaan uit, always paired with uit, so de salade bestaat uit lists its parts.

target: Op de valreep haalde zij nog net de trein.
english: At the last moment she just barely caught the train.
tip: Dutch catches a train with halen: de trein halen, not vangen.

target: Kun je het raam even opendoen want het is benauwd?
english: Can you open the window because it is stuffy?
tip: Want means because but keeps normal word order, so want het is benauwd, unlike omdat which sends the verb to the end.

target: De trein komt over vijf minuten aan op spoor drie.
english: The train arrives in five minutes on platform three.
tip: For time ahead, over means in or from now, so over vijf minuten means in five minutes.
